Buying gift boxes in Japan to take home? Since 1 November 2026, tax-free shopping works differently: you pay the tax at the till and get it back at the airport, and eating one sweet can cost you the whole refund 👇

📌 Save this before your shopping day (the full rules are here) 👉 https://japanbystation.com/depachika-japan-food-halls-how-they-work

✅ THE NEW TAX-FREE CHECKLIST

1️⃣ Spend at least ¥5,000 before tax in the same store on the same day. Food and other items now count together.

2️⃣ Register the purchase at the store's tax-free counter. Some stores take a cut: Takashimaya deducts 23% of the tax amount as a fee.

3️⃣ Keep the boxes together and unopened. If anything from that purchase is missing or eaten when customs checks, nothing on it is refunded.

4️⃣ At the airport, scan your passport at customs before you check your bags, within 90 days of buying. Then the refund is paid out.

5️⃣ Eat the rest. Food you finish in Japan never counted anyway, so the taiyaki for the train is just a taiyaki.

The old sealed plastic bags are gone, which makes the food halls friendlier for gift shopping than before. The catch is simply: don't open the gift box.

👉 Plus the sweets that only come in on set days, and when the evening stickers go on:
